confidence_note: The book's discussion of turning routine work into flow (set own goals, find feedback, bring full attention) is well known; the factory-worker case is taken from the reference text and could not be checked against the book (web search found only secondary summaries; a named assembly-line worker with timing figures appears in Csikszentmihalyi's earlier Flow, not verified for this book). Omitted on purpose: any name, cycle time, count or direct quote; the three questions are paraphrased, not quoted.
facts: Csikszentmihalyi describes a factory worker doing a monotonous, repetitive task: the same movement for hours.
Many workers in that kind of job find it boring, meaningless and draining.
This worker kept setting himself small goals: finish this batch in less time, make fewer errors, be faster this morning than yesterday morning.
Csikszentmihalyi's reading: the worker turned the same task into a flow activity. He set the challenge himself, feedback came instantly, concentration came on its own.
The book presents this as a learnable skill: for any activity ask what could add challenge, how to get immediate feedback, and what brings your full attention to the task.
Flow depends on a person's relationship with the activity, not on the activity itself: the same job can bore one person and absorb another.
scene_details: the same movement repeated for hours
a batch finished against the clock
a comparison between this morning and yesterday morning
tension: Same monotonous job, but most workers find it deadening while this one finds it absorbing.
opening_idea: A line where the hands repeat one movement for hours, and one worker who treats it differently from the rest.

lessons.idea: Give a routine task a target you set yourself and a way to see right away whether you hit it.
lessons.anchor: the worker's own targets for each batch and the instant feedback of finished pieces

reflect_final: Which ordinary task in your week could you give a small target, and how would you see right away whether you reached it?

use_cases.move: Pick one measurable target for the chore today and check it when you finish.

use_cases.situation: A colleague complains the work is pointless.
use_cases.move: Ask what small target they could set on the work itself, like the factory worker who raced the clock on each batch.
Offer a small target, like finishing before a song ends, and compare it with yesterday.

pocket_idea: The factory worker made a repeated movement absorbing by setting his own target and checking each batch.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: The same factory job bored most people and absorbed one worker who kept racing his own morning from the day before.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: Factory worker, repetitive job, others find it deadening, he sets small targets each batch, checks errors and speed against yesterday; Csikszentmihalyi calls it flow made by oneself.
